inventory.observation: One oblique rotational-solid coordinate frame. The x axis runs from left of the origin through three section centers and out beyond the rightmost section, slightly down-right in projection. The y axis is vertical with a positive-up arrow and extends far below origin. A third oblique axis/ray runs down-left through the origin and continues a short way up-right. This is a shared frame, not separate diagrams.

Italic x labels the right axis end and y the upper vertical axis. An oval glyph above-left of origin may be O or 0; no inference is made. There is no clearly readable separate z label at the oblique axis endpoint.

Arrow-over-i-like mark below the positive x-axis near origin, arrow-over-j-like mark left of the positive y axis, and a third compact basis mark by the down-left oblique ray. Exact third letter and exact vector typography are not independently certain.

Two thick solid exterior meridional outlines enclose a widening body about x: an upper outline increases then flattens, and a lower outline falls down-right. Both retain short solid extensions left of the a-section and significant solid extensions beyond the b-section. Neither is hatched. They do not simply stop at the section rims.

Three elliptical transverse sections appear in increasing left-to-right size, centered on the x axis at a, an interior x, and b. Their projected vertical diameters increase with x. At a and interior x, left/near semicircular outlines are solid and right/far semicircular outlines dashed. The rightmost b ellipse has its entire rim solid. The upper and lower extremities of each section meet the upper and lower meridians.

Vertical center/diameter construction lines run from upper to lower meridian in the a, interior x and b sections; dashed center-line pieces are visible. The axial line through interior sections has dashed/hidden portions; it returns to a solid external axis to the right. The interior x and b centers appear emphasized at line intersections; no additional independent point labels are present.

Italic a is just below/right of the small left section center, x below/right of the interior section center, and b below/right of the large right section center. These section labels are different from the x axis name at far right.
Inside the b-section a solid oblique line passes through the b center, from the lower-left rim toward the upper-right rim. It is instructional internal geometry, not a second exterior body outline.

A phi-family angle glyph appears between the small a-section and the interior section near the upper-left interior of the body. Its precise phi-family glyph form is not independently certain. No numeric angle or rotation answer is printed, and no unambiguous curved rotation arrow is visible.

S(x)-like label appears above-left of the intermediate upper rim. A thin leader starts as an underline/horizontal stroke below the label then bends down-right to the intermediate upper section/meridian junction. This association must not migrate to the b-section.

All section centers share the x axis, their planes are transverse to that axis, the two meridians are corresponding upper/lower radial extents, and the oblique diameter at b shows a direction in the same cross-sectional plane. No answer, numerical dimensions, hatching, extra fourth section, or isolated arrow depicting a numerical rotation is present.

sourceModernizationBoundary: A modern oblique projection may regularize geometry, but all three sections, their distinct hidden/visible rim treatment, interior diameter, leader association, shared center axis, and both meridian extensions outside a..b remain source requirements.
